business_scope.primary_industry_name: Cross-Border Physical Consignment of Shredded Non-Ferrous Scrap

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Republic of the Marshall Islands (ISO 3166-1 alpha-3: MHL; input composite_key 'PNG' is a data-entry error, PNG belongs to Papua New Guinea)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid: common-law corporate jurisprudence modeled on the Delaware General Corporation Law, with Marshallese customary law recognized by the Constitution; unitary national system with no sub-state tax distinctions
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Compact of Free Association (COFA) with the United States of America (trade, economic assistance and most-favored-nation elements)
Pacific Agreement on Closer Economic Relations Plus (PACER Plus)
South Pacific Tuna Treaty (multilateral fisheries economic access)
No comprehensive Double Taxation Avoidance Agreement in force; non-resident corporation exemption is sourced in the Income Tax Act 1989

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Business Corporations Act (BCA), Title 51 RMI Revised Code as amended (including 2022 beneficial ownership register provisions); Financial Transactions Reporting Act 2000 (FTRA); Banking Act 1993; Criminal Code Title 31; Mutual Assistance in Criminal Matters Act 2003; RMI Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU) directives; FATF Recommendations R.10, R.12 and R.24 as applied through APG mutual evaluations

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, directors, UBOs, counterparties, consignors and consignees against OFAC SDN, UN Security Council Consolidated Lists (including 1267/1988 ISIL/Al-Qaida), EU Consolidated List, UK HMT Sanctions List, and RMI domestic designations; PEP classification and enhanced due diligence for the 'Medium_Risk_Enhanced' tier assigned to ISIC Rev.4 4669 (wholesale of waste and scrap) / NAICS 2022 423930 (Recycled Metal Merchant Wholesalers); trade-based money-laundering checks, conflict-mineral and OECD Responsible Supply Chain Due Diligence screening for copper scrap origin; FTRA reporting of suspicious transactions to the RMI FIU; five-year record retention.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: RMI Office of the Registrar of Corporations, Majuro (registry operations and name reservations are channeled through licensed registered agents; no unrestricted public search interface exists)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Official languages are Marshallese and English; corporate names must be rendered in English/Latin script with a statutory suffix; no Marshallese transliteration is required; the foreign operating name of the copper scrap trading business must be registered in the counterparty jurisdiction where physical consignment occurs
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: On rejection: submit a fresh application; obtain ministerial approval for sensitive tokens; file a written administrative appeal to the Registrar within 14 business days; if denied, seek judicial review in the RMI High Court under the Administrative Procedure Act; in parallel, reserve the trade name in the jurisdiction of physical scrap consignment.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permitted as a substitute for the statutory registered office; a physical street address in Majuro (normally the licensed registered agent's office) is mandatory at all times under the BCA; remote management of the offshore circular-metals trading business is permissible because the non-resident BC derives no income from within RMI; a mail-forwarding/virtual premise in RMI is not sufficient for registered-office purposes.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low for RMI premises (estimated under 10% annual likelihood absent complaint or FIU/Customs request); the registered agent must produce corporate and UBO records to the Registrar, FIU or law enforcement on lawful demand; at foreign consignment sites, host-jurisdiction customs and scrap-import licensing authorities conduct physical inspections at a materially higher probability (estimated 20%-40% for high-volume consignments).

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Marshall Islands Business Corporations Act (BCA), Title 32 of the RMI Revised Code; Sections 33 (Certificate of Incorporation), 42 (Incorporators), 44 (Execution and Filing), 47 (Registered Office and Registered Agent), 86 (Board of Directors).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Office of the Registrar of Corporations, Majuro Atoll, Republic of the Marshall Islands (submissions accepted directly or through licensed RMI registered agents).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for a Business Corporation; shares may be issued for such consideration as the board determines, including no-par shares. No escrow account, capital deposit, or paid-up proof is required for non-resident entities.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the subscription for 100 no-par value ordinary shares is accepted, and the Corporate Secretary is directed to issue share certificates upon payment of the agreed consideration. FURTHER RESOLVED, that the registered office located with the licensed registered agent in Majuro, Marshall Islands, as stated in the Certificate of Incorporation, is adopted. FURTHER RESOLVED, that John Doe is appointed Chief Executive Officer, Jane Doe as Secretary, and Richard Roe as Treasurer, each to serve at the pleasure of the Board. FURTHER RESOLVED, that the officers are authorized to open bank accounts, negotiate documentary letters of credit, and execute all contracts for cross-border consignment of recycled copper scrap.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Office of the Registrar of Corporations, Majuro (online name search via the RMI corporate registry portal or through a licensed RMI registered agent)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct an availability search and reserve the proposed corporate name with the suffix Corporation, Incorporated, or Limited. Submit the name reservation application in English together with the registered agent consent. The reservation is effective for 60 calendar days.
required_dossiers: Copy of incorporator passport or national identification
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected or confusingly similar, the registered agent files a substitute name reservation within two business days; the filing fee is not forfeited if the name is corrected in the Certificate of Incorporation before formal submission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Execution of Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Incorporator(s) and licensed RMI registered agent (Corporation Trust Center, Majuro)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Certificate of Incorporation stating the corporate name, registered office and agent, authorized share structure, and unrestricted lawful business purpose. Each incorporator signs before a notary public, and the registered agent executes the consent to act as agent.
required_dossiers: Registered agent consent and acceptance form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar queries the purpose clause or share structure, a Certificate of Amendment under BCA Section 66 is prepared and refiled; corrected execution pages are re-notarized and resubmitted within five business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory Filing with the Registrar of Corporations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Office of the Registrar of Corporations, Majuro Atoll, Republic of the Marshall Islands
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the notarized Certificate of Incorporation with the Registrar together with the official state filing fee of US$250. Upon endorsement, obtain the stamped Certificate of Incorporation and certified true copies for banking, licensing, and counterparty purposes.
required_dossiers: Official filing fee receipt of US$250
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is refused or queried, the Registrar issues a written notice of defect; the defect is cured by a corrective filing under BCA Section 44(6). Clerical omissions are refiled within five business days without an additional fee, unless the corporate name is changed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Organizational Board Meeting and Share Subscription
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors acting by unanimous written consent or by duly convened organizational meeting
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The initial directors adopt the Pro-Forma First Board Resolution, accepting the share subscription, adopting the registered office, appointing officers, and authorizing banking signatories. Minutes or unanimous written consent is entered into the corporate records and maintained by the registered agent.
required_dossiers: Unanimous written consent or organizational board minutes
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If an appointment is challenged under conflict-of-interest provisions, the board ratifies the action by a subsequent resolution or the shareholders execute a written consent under BCA Section 88; corrected documents are endorsed with a retroactive timestamp.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Non-Resident Tax Status Registration and Bank Account Establishment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Finance – Tax and Revenue (TRE), Republic of the Marshall Islands; licensed international banking institution
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Declare non-resident status to the TRE to obtain written confirmation of non-applicability of income tax on offshore trading income; register a tax identification number if any domestic event occurs. Submit certified corporate documents to a licensed bank to open a corporate account with Documentary LC and Swift TT facilities.
required_dossiers: Register of directors, officers, and shareholders
Passports and proof of address for directors, officers, and beneficial owners
Bank account opening forms and AML/KYC declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank imposes enhanced KYC queries due to the medium-risk AML classification of scrap trading, the entity provides a consolidated registry extract, supply contract stack, and a board resolution confirming no onshore commercial activity in the RMI; a substitute licensed bank may be engaged if the first institution declines.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Foreign Investment Board, Ministry of Commerce, Investment and Trade; Marshall Islands Environmental Protection Authority (RMI EPA)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Foreign Investment Business License (FIBL) for Cross-Border Wholesale Consignment of Recycled Non-Ferrous Scrap (ISIC 4669 / NAICS 423930)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Marshall Islands Environmental Protection Authority (RMI EPA)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category 3 – Registration/Exempt: no full EIA report is required for pure consignment trading without local processing or warehousing; a simplified EPA registration form is lodged to document transboundary movement where shredded copper scrap transits RMI ports.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Stormwater runoff suspended solids shall not exceed 50 mg/L; zero point-source wastewater discharge from any staging area; sealed containment for leachate capture; prohibition of open burning; compliance with Basel Convention notification for transboundary movement of non-hazardous copper scrap and MARPOL Annex V waste segregation.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: A non-resident trading company without physical premises in the RMI is exempt from initial fire and structural filing. If a liaison office or port-side warehouse is later established, a fire safety certificate from Majuro Fire and Emergency Services, a structural load clearance for racking systems, and an Occupational Safety and Health clearance from the RMI Ministry of Health and Human Services are required, with a 30-day compliance window.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Marshall Islands Revenue and Customs Office (RICO), Ministry of Finance, Republic of the Marshall Islands, Majuro and Ebeye service offices. Corporate formation and annual filing are administered by the Registrar of Corporations, Ministry of Finance, a separate division from RICO. No mandatory e-filing portal exists for non-resident exempt business corporations; filings are effected through licensed registered agents.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A non-resident Business Corporation (BC) is not required to procure a TIN, VAT ID, or GRT number solely for offshore trading activity. If the BC later engages in business within the Republic of the Marshall Islands (RMI), the following sequence applies: (1) file for a Foreign Investment Business License (FIBL) under the Foreign Investment Business Act 1998 unless wholly owned by RMI citizens; (2) register with RICO for Gross Revenue Tax in the prescribed registration form; (3) receive a RICO-issued GRT/TIN; (4) file periodic GRT returns and remit tax on annual gross revenue exceeding USD 25,000; and (5) obtain any municipal business license required by local ordinance. For a pure offshore consignment business operating through documentary letters of credit and SWIFT TT payment rails, no RMI tax registration is triggered.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: The RMI has no 'check-the-box' or statutory hybrid-mismatch election under domestic law. Entity classification is fixed by the Business Corporation Act (BCA); a BC is a body corporate separate from its shareholders. The only practical elections are: (a) maintenance of non-resident status versus conducting RMI domestic business, which would subject the BC to GRT and business licensing; (b) charter elections under the BCA regarding corporate purpose and capital structure, which have no effect on RMI tax classification. For foreign purposes, particularly US federal tax, the BC is a per se eligible entity that may be affirmatively classified as an association taxable as a corporation or disregarded under Treasury Regulation Section 301.7701-3, but such election does not alter RMI domestic tax status.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: No VAT, GST, or sales-and-use tax regime exists in the Republic of the Marshall Islands. The only consumption-type indirect taxation is Import Duty levied under the RMI Customs Tariff Schedule, with general ad valorem rates typically between 5% and 10% and specific rates up to 100% for certain goods. The Gross Revenue Tax (3% standard rate; 7% for certain telecommunications services) is best characterized as a direct turnover tax on RMI-source revenue rather than an indirect tax for VAT/GST analogy purposes.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: USD 25,000 annual gross revenue derived from RMI sources is the statutory GRT registration and liability threshold. For import duty, no monetary threshold applies; liability arises per transaction when goods physically enter the RMI customs territory. A FIBL, with annual fees generally ranging from USD 250 to USD 5,000 depending on business scope, is required before commencing any foreign investment business in the RMI. Non-resident BCs without RMI-source operations are below all registration thresholds.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: The RMI has not enacted any mandatory electronic invoicing, real-time fiscal clearance, API reporting, or digital stamping regime. RICO Customs operates on paper and PDF-based declarations, manifests, and import/export entry forms. Commercial invoices and packing lists are seller-generated without pre-clearance validation by the tax authority. A cross-border consignment of shredded scrap copper that does not touch RMI territory is outside all RMI fiscal clearance procedures.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Not applicable. The Republic of the Marshall Islands does not impose VAT or GST; therefore the concept of zero-rating, export VAT refunds, or input-output reconciliation has no statutory meaning in RMI law. Exports from the RMI, and offshore consignments such as the underlying ISIC 4669 scrap-copper trade, are outside the scope of RMI taxation. The documentation bundle must instead satisfy the importing jurisdiction's customs and VAT/duty regimes, the governing letter-of-credit conditions, and the bank's trade-compliance and sanctions due process.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (required only where RMI export clearance is triggered; for pure offshore transshipment, an internal export manifest may suffice)
Bill of Lading (or multimodal transport document evidencing physical consignment from origin to destination)

Inward Remittance Certificate / SWIFT MT103 confirmation (commercially required under documentary LC and TT payment rails; not a statutory RMI requirement because the RMI uses the US dollar and imposes no exchange controls)
Commercial Invoice and Packing List (LC-compliant and matched to the transport document)
Independent Weight Certificate and Assay Certificate for recycled scrap copper (substantiating quantity, copper content, and absence of prohibited contaminants)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Zero-rating clawback is structurally impossible because no export VAT is charged in the RMI. However, analogous risks apply: customs misdeclaration or undervaluation in RMI territory attracts forfeiture of goods, fines up to double the duty evaded, and criminal liability for false statements. A BC that falsely claims non-resident status while conducting RMI business is subject to GRT reassessment, statutory interest, late-payment penalties, potential FIBL revocation, and corporate-registry sanctions. Given the ISIC 4669 medium-risk AML profile, fabricated invoices, weight mismatches, or inconsistent assay documentation may also generate a Suspicious Transaction Report to the RMI Financial Intelligence Unit and correspondent-bank de-risking.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: The Republic of the Marshall Islands maintains no domestic central bank. The U.S. dollar is the official legal tender under the Compact of Free Association, making the U.S. Federal Reserve the de facto monetary and settlement authority. Prudential licensing, regulation, and AML/CFT supervision of the banking sector is vested in the Financial Institutions Commission (FIC), established under the Financial Institutions Act 2020 (FIA 2020), which succeeded the Banking Commissioner of the Ministry of Finance. The relevant clearing and control environment for this non-resident Business Corporation (BC) is therefore U.S.-centric, executed through FIC-licensed banks (Bank of Marshall Islands and Bank of Guam, RMI branch) and their U.S. correspondent clearings.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Because the functional and settlement currency is the USD, statutory exchange control is functionally null. There are no capital account restrictions, no repatriation approval regime, and no dual-currency mechanism: equity injection, profit remittance, liquidation surplus, and third-party trade settlements may all be cleared freely in USD. Real-world friction is limited to (i) correspondent-bank de-risking of Pacific island banks, (ii) FIA 2020 customer due-diligence obligations applicable to non-resident BCs, and (iii) transaction monitoring thresholds enforced by the RMI Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU); none of these requires a separate central-bank foreign-investment permit or capital controls waiver.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None exist. RMI imposes no statutory timeline, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no surrender-to-domestic-bank obligation on export proceeds from recycled scrap copper. Proceeds may be retained offshore, swept to the BOMI operational account, or applied directly against supplier settlements; the only compliance touchpoints are (i) accurate reconciliation of each receipt to the MT103 reference narrative and HS 7404 commodity description, (ii) 5-year retention of trade documents under FIA 2020, and (iii) filing of suspicious transaction reports (STRs) with the RMI FIU where any proceeds derive from suspicious counterparty activity.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Bank of Marshall Islands (BOMI) - Main Branch, Majuro
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Operational Account (segregated USD demand ledger; initial equity tranches are escrowed pending FIC source-of-funds clearance before operational activation)

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Bank of Guam - Republic of the Marshall Islands Branch, Majuro
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account / Trade Settlement Account (USD demand account with direct access to Bank of Guam's U.S. clearing network for MT103 outbound wires and MT700 documentary credit operations)
Not applicable - development lender only; no transactional deposit, FX, or trade-facilitation product

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low for offshore digital EMI wallet providers. FIA 2020 makes it an offense to operate a deposit-taking or e-money business without an RMI license, and licensed banks are required to treat relationships with unlicensed EMIs as an AML red flag. A non-resident BC should not rely on Panama, BVI, or Hong Kong electronic money institution cards for treasury flows. Ancillary collections may use regulated U.S. money-transmitter platforms, but statutory payment rails for scrap copper trade must be SWIFT MT103/MT700 documentary instruments through FIC-licensed institutions.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In-person KYC interview is mandatory for at least one authorized signatory at the opening branch in Majuro; fully remote opening is only available where the signatory already holds a KYC-complete relationship at Bank of Guam or BOMI with a branch-attested signature card. Alternatively, the BC's directors may appoint a resident RMI-licensed corporate service provider to hold a joint-signing mandate with an authorized director, subject to a videoconference confirmation of identity conducted by the bank's compliance officer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Red Flag 1 - Scrap metal merchant classification (ISIC 4669 / NAICS 423930): trade-based money laundering (TBML) typologies flag invoice vs weight mismatches against LME copper prices, cash-equivalent settlement, and payments through unlisted intermediary accounts.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (a) Fully executed supply and off-take agreements; (b) LME-based pricing formula per shipment with independent assay and weight certificates from SGS, Bureau Veritas, or Intertek; (c) original bills of lading, packing lists, and port weighbridge tickets; (d) written confirmation that supplier counterparties hold valid downstream recycler qualifications (e.g., Chinese import registration under GB/T 38470-2019 for recycled copper raw materials); (e) board-adopted trade management manual banning cash, bearer instruments, and third-party payment instructions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Red Flag 2 - Non-resident tax-exempt BC in a small-island jurisdiction with a history of EU AML/CFT watch-listing and APG mutual-evaluation follow-up, creating correspondent de-risking exposure at U.S. and Asian clearing banks.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (a) Registrar of Corporations certificate of good standing; (b) FIC-compliant beneficial ownership registry extract showing each ultimate beneficial owner; (c) economic substance evidence: physical office sublease in Majuro, local registered agent engagement, corporate records maintained at the registered office, and board minutes evidencing RMI situs; (d) audited or reviewed management accounts of the trading BC demonstrating actual transactions rather than passive shell activity; (e) a written AML/CFT manual with an appointed compliance officer and a 5-year record retention policy.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Red Flag 3 - Opacity in inbound funding where equity or shareholder loans arrive from another offshore or related entity, typical of privately held commodity SPVs.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (a) Notarized shareholders loan agreement or board resolution approving share issuance with stated size, subscription price, and tenor; (b) source-of-wealth memorandum per beneficial owner with independent evidence such as asset sale deeds, dividend vouchers, or liquidation statements; (c) six months of bank statements of the remitting account; (d) statutory declaration that funds do not derive from criminal proceeds under RMI anti-money laundering legislation; (e) irrevocable undertaking to notify the bank and the FIU on any subsequent off-book settlement detected by compliance monitoring.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity or shareholder loan funding must arrive in USD by SWIFT from the investor's own bank account, with a narrative containing the BC's exact legal name, ISIC 4669 recycled copper trading capital, and a reference to the RMI board resolution; the receiving bank credits a segregated Capital Escrow Account until source-of-funds documents are cleared by compliance. The standard purpose-code mapping used by U.S. correspondents is 'G3' (external short-term loans) for shareholder advances; capital subscription entries are booked with a corporate-purpose narrative because RMI is not an IMF-code reporting jurisdiction. Physical import or export of cash above USD 10,000 across RMI borders triggers currency declaration obligations; the BC must never inject funds via cash, travelers cheques, or third-party settlement agents.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlements must move through dual rails: (1) SWIFT MT103 direct payment for consignments under USD 250,000, instructed only upon receipt of a scanned bill of lading, assay certificate, seller-signed proforma invoice, and per-lot weight certificate; (2) irrevocable unconfirmed or confirmed documentary letter of credit (MT700) for larger consignments, with a document checklist of commercial invoice, full set of original bills of lading, weight and assay certificate, and certificate of origin, payable at sight through Bank of Guam's U.S. network; a standby LC (MT760) may secure supplier performance bonds; interbank funding sweeps between BOMI and U.S. correspondents are executed via MT202. Every narrative must embed the HS code 7404 (copper waste and scrap) and the ISIC 4669 purpose code to avoid false-positive sanctions screening in the Asia-Pacific clearing corridor.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: None required for USD-functional operations: recycled copper wire is globally priced in USD via LME copper contracts, and both BOMI and Bank of Guam accounts are USD-denominated, eliminating balance-sheet FX exposure.

Deliverable USD/CNY forward (tenor at or below 90 days, aligned to each physical shipment cycle) executed via Bank of Guam or a licensed Chinese or Hong Kong bank where a mainland supplier insists on CNY invoices.
USD/EUR deliverable forward for that portion of scrap off-take sold to German or Italian recyclers where settlement in EUR is contractually required.
LME-cleared copper swap or CME Copper futures in a segregated margin account for commodity price hedging; not an FX instrument, but permissible and recommended to lock input-cost spreads.

Cross-currency swap (USD/CNY or USD/EUR, tenor exceeding six months) permitted only with an OECD-licensed banking counterparty under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement; RMI-licensed banks do not act as swap counterparties.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Report under Section 93 of the Business Corporations Act (corporate registry return confirming directors, officers, registered office, registered agent, and share capital)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Republic of the Marshall Islands
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before the anniversary of the date of incorporation; when the anniversary falls on a non-business day, the deadline moves to the next business day
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Registrar may impose a late-filing penalty and, after written notice and continued default, administratively dissolve or strike off the corporation; directors and officers remain liable for unlawful continuation

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory audit is required for a non-resident, non-public Business Corporation; the Marshall Islands BCA imposes no revenue, asset, employee, or shareholder threshold triggering audit. Audit is required only for licensed banks, licensed insurers or reinsurers, and exchange-listed entities.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: No prescribed local GAAP; books and records may be maintained under IFRS or US GAAP as adopted by management; audited financial statements are not filed with the Registrar unless required under a financing or contractual covenant.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The Marshall Islands does not mandate a separate UBO annual filing. The registered agent conducts an annual reconciliation and audit of the Register of Members and share-transfer documentation under AML/KYC obligations; the Annual Report confirms directors and officers, while ultimate beneficial ownership is recorded in the agent's confidential AML file and disclosed to the Registrar or law-enforcement agencies only on lawful demand.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 750 - USD 1,500 per annum for registered office, resident agent, and corporate secretarial services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 0 when no audit is required; voluntary certified audit typically USD 4,000 - USD 8,000 depending on transaction volume and consolidation

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% (RMI imposes no corporate income tax on non-resident Business Corporations; tax is limited to income derived from sources within the Marshall Islands)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Non-resident Business Corporations are structurally exempt from Marshall Islands income tax, withholding tax, and capital gains tax. There are no statutory tax holidays or preferential deductions; the exemption is automatic provided the corporation does not carry on business in RMI.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: No corporate income tax return is issued. The legally equivalent annual filing for a non-resident BC is the Annual Corporation Registration Renewal (Annual Report and Statement of Authorization), submitted to the RMI Registrar of Corporations through the MARLIN online portal (Marshalls On-line Registration and Information Network).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The renewal and payment of the annual franchise fee are due on or before May 31 of each year for corporations on a calendar fiscal year, or within four months after the fiscal year-end for corporations with a non-calendar fiscal year. Late filings are accepted, but defaults trigger penalties and administrative dissolution after 120 days.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box A - Entity Name and Registered Number
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: The exact legal name of the Business Corporation as stated in its Certificate of Incorporation, followed by its RMI registration number (e.g., MH-2014-1234).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the full legal name only; do not enter trade names or DBA designations. Any mismatch invalidates the filing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box B - Registered Office in RMI
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Physical street address of the registered office maintained by the licensed resident agent in Majuro or Ebeye.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A P.O. Box is insufficient unless accompanied by a physical location. The registered office must be operational during normal business hours.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box C - Resident Agent Name and Address
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Identity of the RMI-licensed registered agent appointed by the corporation, including the agent's license number and full business address.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident BC must maintain a licensed registered agent at all times. Any change of agent must be pre-filed with the Registrar before the renewal.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box D - Fiscal Year End Date
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: The date on which the corporation's financial year ends (default: December 31).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: This date is purely administrative for the corporate register. It has no income tax consequence for a tax-exempt non-resident BC.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box E - Authorized Share Capital and Franchise Fee Computation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total number of authorized shares and the corresponding annual franchise fee tier in US dollars (e.g., US$100 for capitalization up to US$100,000; US$150 up to US$1,000,000; US$250 up to US$5,000,000; US$300 up to US$10,000,000; US$400 up to US$50,000,000).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Declare authorized capital accurately. Under-declaration to reduce the fee is treated as a false filing and attracts penalties. Fees are payable in US dollars.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box F - Certificate of Exemption / Non-Resident Status Declaration
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statutory declaration confirming that the corporation has derived no income from sources within the Republic of the Marshall Islands during the tax year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: This declaration is mandatory for non-resident BCs claiming tax-exempt status. Signing a false declaration constitutes perjury and may result in revocation of the corporate charter and personal liability.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of the annual renewal attracts an administrative penalty equal to 10% of the applicable franchise fee per month or part thereof, up to a maximum equal to the fee. If the renewal remains unfiled for 120 days, the Registrar may administratively dissolve the corporation. Reinstatement requires payment of a US$500 fee plus all arrears and penalties. Operating while dissolved makes the corporation and its directors liable for trading without legal personality.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% - The Republic of the Marshall Islands does not levy withholding tax on dividends paid by a non-resident Business Corporation, whether paid to resident or non-resident shareholders.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: RMI maintains no meaningful double tax agreement network. Because withholding tax is nil, no RMI DTA relief is required. To support foreign tax credit claims or exemption evidence in other jurisdictions, a non-resident BC should obtain a Certificate of Non-Residence from the RMI Ministry of Finance and a Certificate of Good Standing from the Registrar. The standard protocol is: (1) file a written request with the Ministry of Finance and Registrar; (2) remit the administrative service fee (US$100); (3) attach an affidavit or PRC-audited statement confirming no RMI source income; (4) receive the certificate, valid for one year, for submission to foreign tax authorities as country-of-residence proof.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory RMI withholding tax on royalties and debt interest paid by a non-resident BC is 0%. There are no treaty rates because no relevant comprehensive income tax treaty exists; foreign-source payments remain outside RMI's territorial taxation.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Not applicable. RMI has no corporate income tax and therefore no statutory Local File or Master File documentation threshold. The Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) require all relevant entities to maintain adequate records of core income-generating activities in RMI, but no specific TP threshold is prescribed in US dollars (the local currency is the US dollar).
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The RMI Economic Substance Regulations 2019 (as amended) apply to corporations carrying out 'relevant activities', which include distribution and service centers. The PCR/consignment sale of shredded non-ferrous scrap metals (ISIC 4669) is a distribution activity where the BC purchases goods, manages physical consignment, and resells to third parties. The BC must in each financial year satisfy: (1) board meetings and strategic decisions held in RMI; (2) physical premises and a minimum number of qualified employees at a level commensurate with the activity; (3) adequate expenditure in RMI; and (4) performance of core income-generating activities — purchasing, inventory management, transportation coordination, and risk management — in RMI, unless outsourced to a qualifying RMI entity. Annual economic substance reporting is mandatory. Non-compliance fines range from US$10,000 to US$50,000 per offence, with a possible additional daily fine and strike-off.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: A non-resident BC deriving income from RMI sources (e.g., freight from RMI ports or trading with an RMI resident) while repeatedly declaring itself fully tax-exempt, or falsifying the registered office and agent address to conceal the actual center of management.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Income Tax Act renders tax evasion a criminal offense punishable by a fine of up to US$10,000 and imprisonment for up to five years. The Business Corporations Act separately imposes fines of up to US$5,000 for false declarations and permits immediate cancellation of registration.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Any director or officer who signs a false statutory declaration or knowingly submits a false annual report is personally liable for all uncollected taxes, penalties, and costs. Criminal conviction for evasion carries imprisonment; the courts may also issue a travel ban against the director pending restitution.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company Abuse / Economic Substance Failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the non-resident BC purely as an invoicing shell with no RMI management, no substance, and no legitimate commercial justification for the consignment sales, while retaining profits overseas to shield them from foreign tax authorities.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Economic Substance Regulations fines: US$10,000 per offense for failure to provide information; US$20,000 per offense for false or misleading information; US$50,000 for continuing failure after formal notice. The Registrar may strike the entity off the register and issue a warning to banking partners.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of a sham entity face disqualification from acting as directors for up to 15 years and personal fines equal to double the entity-level fine. Civil restitution orders may require directors to repatriate profits earned through the lack of substance.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting proceeds from scrap copper wire sourced from stolen or sanctioned entities, or structuring documentary LC and Swift TT payments to disguise the origin of funds, lack of due diligence on counterparties, or funneling payments through transit accounts in breach of AML obligations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The RMI Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Act imposes imprisonment up to 15 years and fines up to US$250,000 for money laundering. The Financial Intelligence Unit may freeze bank accounts, block LC payments, and recommend criminal prosecution. Violations of UN or US sanctions incorporated into RMI law attract seizure of goods and forfeiture of assets.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are criminally liable if they knew or should have known that consignment proceeds were derived from illegal activity; individual liability carries mandatory imprisonment. Civil director liability extends to receiving and forwarding tainted funds, including disgorgement and legal costs.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Trading in recycled non-ferrous scrap without the required RMI business license or relevant commodity trading license when such transactions involve storage, import, export, or port calls in Marshall Islands territory.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Operating without a license is a misdemeanor under RMI trade and commerce regulations, punishable by a fine of US$500 to US$5,000 per day of violation. The regulator may void affected sale and shipping contracts and deny future license applications.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are jointly and severally liable for each day of unlicensed operation, and the corporation may forfeit all revenues earned during the unlicensed period. Individual directors may be ordered to pay treble damages to indemnify the RMI government.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Corporate Veil Piercing / Trading While Dissolved
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Continuing to execute purchase orders, LC negotiations, and TT settlements for scrap metal after administrative dissolution for non-payment of annual fees, or commencing liquidation without preserving creditor claims and statutory notice.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Contracts entered into while administratively dissolved are voidable at the counterparty's option. The Registrar imposes a reinstatement fee of US$500 plus all unpaid fees and penalties. Fraudulent continuation of business during dissolution may result in unlimited liability for all debts incurred during the period.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers are personally liable for obligations incurred after the dissolution date, without limit. The RMI courts may pierce the corporate veil to impose personal bankruptcy, freeze personal assets, impose a travel ban prohibiting departure from the country, and order imprisonment for willful violations of the Business Corporations Act.
